reason: The text is fundamentally structured around and reinforces strict hierarchies at multiple levels: (1) Divine hierarchy - God commands Moses, who executes God's will; (2) Institutional hierarchy - Pharaoh commands his servants and people; (3) The entire narrative arc depends on enforcing hierarchical obedience - God's authority must be recognized and submitted to. The magicians' failure and inability to stand before Moses demonstrates a collapse of the magicians' status within the hierarchy. The repeated formula 'וַיְחַזֵּק יְהוָה אֶת־ לֵב פַּרְעֹה' (God hardened Pharaoh's heart) shows God's supreme authority over Pharaoh's will. Rather than discouraging hierarchy, the text actively employs and validates strict hierarchical structures as the mechanism through which divine will is accomplished.
